cards.front: What are the two kinds of nested class in Java?
cards.back: Static nested classes and non-static inner classes
cards.extra: A static nested class is a member like any other static member; an inner class carries a hidden reference to its outer instance.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::05 Nested Classes

cards.back: A loop inside the body of another loop
cards.extra: The inner loop runs to completion for every single iteration of the outer one, so the counts multiply.

cards.front: Which stream writes objects so they can be read back?
cards.back: ObjectOutputStream writes; ObjectInputStream reads
cards.extra: The class must implement Serializable, or you get a NotSerializableException at write time.

cards.back: The order in which operators in an expression are evaluated
cards.extra: a + b * c multiplies first. Parentheses override it, and when in doubt you should use them.

cards.back: The same entity — method, operator or object — behaving differently depending on context
cards.extra: For methods it means the call is dispatched by the object's runtime type, not the variable's declared type.

cards.front: What does PrintStream do differently from other output streams?
cards.back: Writes text rather than raw bytes, and converts values to readable form
cards.extra: System.out is a PrintStream. It never throws IOException — it sets an internal error flag instead.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.back: A heap, so elements come out in sorted order rather than insertion order
cards.extra: poll() returns the smallest (natural order) or the one your Comparator ranks first.

cards.back: A first-in, first-out collection; it extends Collection
cards.extra: offer/add to enqueue, poll/remove and peek/element to inspect — the two method sets differ only in how they report failure.

cards.back: The abstract superclass of streams of characters
cards.extra: It is to char data what InputStream is to bytes; you use a concrete subclass such as FileReader or StringReader.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: What must a recursive method have to terminate?
cards.back: A base case that returns without recursing
cards.extra: Without one the calls nest until the stack overflows with StackOverflowError.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::02 Attributes and Methods

cards.back: Inspecting and manipulating classes, constructors, methods and fields at run time
cards.extra: Everything goes through the Class object: getDeclaredMethods, newInstance, invoke.

cards.front: What is Scanner for, and which package is it in?
cards.back: Reading input from streams, files and strings — java.util
cards.extra: hasNext/next per token, plus typed methods like nextInt. It is convenient but slow — not for large files.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: What three things must a singleton class do?
cards.back: Private constructor, a private static instance, and a public static accessor
cards.extra: The constructor prevents new instances; the accessor hands out the one that exists.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.back: Elements kept in sorted order, with first, last, headSet, tailSet views
cards.extra: TreeSet implements it. Elements need natural order or a Comparator.

cards.back: Keys kept sorted, with firstKey, lastKey and range views
cards.extra: TreeMap implements it; NavigableMap extends it with nearest-match lookups.

cards.back: LIFO — last in, first out: push adds to the top, pop removes from the top
cards.extra: It extends Vector, which is why it is synchronized and considered legacy; prefer Deque.

cards.front: What is a static nested class able to do that an inner class cannot?
cards.back: Be instantiated without an outer instance
cards.extra: new Outer.Nested() works; an inner class needs outer.new Inner() because it carries the outer reference.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::05 Nested Classes

cards.back: Accessing a member without creating an instance of the class
cards.extra: Static members belong to the class itself and are shared by every object.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::04 Static Keyword

cards.front: How is a String written in source code?
cards.back: Between double quotes: "hello"
cards.extra: Single quotes are for a char literal, which holds exactly one character.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.back: The superclass: its members are reachable as super.method() and its constructor as super(...)
cards.extra: Needed when a subclass overrides a method but still wants the parent behaviour, or when the parent has no no-arg constructor.

cards.front: How many times is a switch expression evaluated?
cards.back: Once — then compared against each case value
cards.extra: That is the difference from an if-else chain, where every condition is re-evaluated in turn.

cards.front: What does the ternary operator replace?
cards.back: A simple if...else that assigns or returns a value
cards.extra: cond ? a : b is an expression, so it can be used inline — which an if statement cannot.

cards.back: The current object — the instance the method was called on
cards.extra: Used to disambiguate a field from a parameter, and to call another constructor as this(...).
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What is the difference between throw and throws?
cards.back: throw raises an exception; throws declares that a method may raise one
cards.extra: Checked exceptions must be declared in the signature or caught; unchecked ones need not be.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::01 Exception Handling

cards.back: Entries ordered by key, so iteration is sorted
cards.extra: Same tree structure as TreeSet; lookups are O(log n) rather than O(1).

cards.back: Abnormal termination of the program: the catch block handles the exception and flow continues
cards.extra: Without it, an uncaught exception ends the thread and prints the stack trace.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::01 Exception Handling

cards.back: Closes every declared resource automatically at the end of the statement
cards.extra: The resource must implement AutoCloseable. Closes happen in reverse order of declaration, even if the body throws.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::01 Exception Handling

cards.back: Converting a value from one data type to another
cards.extra: Widening (int to long) is automatic; narrowing (double to int) needs an explicit cast and can lose data.

cards.back: A named location in memory that holds a value
cards.extra: Declared with a type, then assigned. The type fixes what can be stored and what operations are legal.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::07 Variables and Scopes

cards.front: What is the difference between ArrayList and Vector?
cards.back: Vector is synchronized; ArrayList is not
cards.extra: Both are resizable arrays. Vector's locking makes it slower and is rarely what you want — use ArrayList and synchronize explicitly.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::04 Collections::02 Array vs ArrayList

cards.back: They are held by weak references, so an entry disappears once nothing else refers to its key
cards.extra: Used for caches and metadata that must not keep objects alive.

cards.front: What are the wrapper classes for?
cards.back: Converting each of the eight primitives into an object
cards.extra: Integer, Long, Short, Byte, Double, Float, Character, Boolean — needed for generics, collections and null representation.
